title: A cash-secured put and a covered call are the same trade
summary: With the same strike and expiry, a cash-secured put and a covered call have the same risk, return and exposure. Put-call parity makes them one payoff. The speaker models both in his P&L calculator: as time decays, the two lines move together as one. The only differences are operational.

steps.caption: The stock trades at $100. Both trades use the $100 strike and the same 30-day expiry.
The covered call: long 100 shares, short one call. Gains are capped, losses run as the stock falls.
The cash-secured put: short one put. Its curve sits on top of the covered call curve.
The difference is about zero at every price. Put-call parity makes them one trade.
Both break even at the strike minus the premium collected.

takeaways: Same strike and same expiry: a covered call and a cash-secured put have the same risk and return.
As time passes the two P&L curves move together.
The differences are operational, such as dividends, assignment and how capital is held.
caveats: Small differences from interest and dividends exist in practice. The calculator shown in the video is the speaker's own tool.
